My gun range has an ever-rotating selection of rental guns, and as a member rentals are free so I have access to an ever-changing, random selection of new guns to try out.

Today I discovered Chiappa Firearms' Rhino series of revolvers - specifically the 200D, a 2" snub-nose. Their primary selling point is that they fire from the **bottom cylinder**, not the top. Chiappa claims that this greatly reduces recoil and kick-up while at the same time making it easier to point at your target, on account of putting the shot more in line with the shooter's arm.

They're about as pretty as a Rhino, too, with a hexagonal cylinder and (rounded) angles everywhere - which means I really, really like the aesthetics as rounded angles are probably the prettiest aesthetic, in my opinion.

* [Right Side](https://i.sli.mg/8YIAAm.jpg) * [Chamber Open](https://i.sli.mg/HwObWz.jpg)

It shot way more accurately than a 2" snub-nose had any business shooting at [10 yards](https://i.sli.mg/aLZoCF.jpg). Given that I'd never shot this gun before, hadn't had a chance to learn its sights, and only put 50 rounds through it in all, I was impressed. It's sadly much more accurate than [my 9mm Pit Bull](https://voat.co/v/guns/comments/828754).

It also articulated like a dream - everything was precise, slick, smooth, and quiet. It was the smoothest gun I've ever shot.

However, there are two major quibbles that would prevent me from buying one as my next gun:

**The Trigger**

I can't actually find the 200D on Chiappa's website - only the [200DS](http://www.chiappafirearms.com/product/725). Note that there is a hammer present - on the 200D that I fired, there was no hammer, so the gun could *only* be fired double-action. The trigger pull was OK but it was a smooth, even pull all the way to the back until it fired. On my Pit Bull, there is a slight click/catch that you can feel that happens when the cylinder has rotated into place to fire, and any further pull will discharge. This allows bringing the gun roughly to bear on target, a half-pull of the trigger to essentially "cock" it, and then a featherweight additional pull to discharge, similar to the trigger pull in single-action mode.

I don't like that I can't do this with this gun. Maybe the model with the exposed hammer would differ, but the even, smooth trigger pull along the whole length made it hard to tell when I had finished rotating the cylinder and when I was cocking the hammer and when the hammer was going to release - leading to getting off-target a bit. It was, in my opinion, *too smooth*.

**The Rear Sights**

[Sights](https://i.sli.mg/fknDRg.jpg)

The front sights were a wonderful, centered fiber-optic red dot. The rear sights, however, were very wide, and I had to visually compare the left and right gaps after centering the post between them - whereas with a narrower channel it would be immediately obvious if they were centered. This took a bit of getting used-to to use effectively, and was particularly distracting at close-range when more of the target could be seen in the empty space around the center post.

---------- **Overall**

Ridiculously smooth, admirably accurate, with a unique aesthetic: the gun's got form *and* function.

I'd have to try the normal 200DS with an exposed hammer to see if it's got the tactile feedback I like. If it does, it'll be the first-place contender for my CCW.

I'm also loving the aesthetic of their [6" Rhino](http://www.chiappafirearms.com/sites/default/files/Rhino6_Nera_0.jpg), though my local range didn't have one of those for rent... I'm probably going to get one.

Work 7 days a week normally. Party in-between at least 3. Respectable job. No benefits. And just enough spending money to destract myself.

Sunlight peers thru the curtains, it's time to start another day.

Throw off the covers and reach for my glasses. Hit the bathroom for a nice huge piss, maybe pinch a loaf if I had too much for dinner last night. Brush the night off my eyes and teeth, detangle the hair.

Plug in the iron, scratch my ass and balls while I decide which shirt to wear. Temporarily forgo a decision and tip toe over piles of clothes, towels and shoes into the kitchen. Open those curtains and let some light hit the plants. Feel bad they have to wait to get up until I do.

Go turn off the radio alarm, which is sounding back in the bedroom, feel lightly depressed how the song playing is relevant. Realize the place smells and throw open some windows on the way. Make another mental note to fix the toilet, it's making that noise again. Stop to watch the birds throw seed from the feeder on the balcony and hop around. Decide on a shirt, look for pants that match. Remember to charge up the cellphone. Check the weather forecast while looking for the plug and decide if walking, biking or driving to work.

Hit the kitchen again for some kefir and supplements. Reishi, cordyceps, chlorella, maca, blue-green algae. Drink a big swig of water, maybe two. Notice a plant going dry, rinse a beer glass in the sink and water it. Bag up the trash, that's what stinks. Scrub the sink quickly, still dirty but not so bad now.

Grab the finishing touches, hat, gloves, shoes, jacket, wallet, keys. Turn off the lights, don't need them now anyway. Prep the bike or car depending on the day. Remember to stretch at the last minute. Play that song from last night on the way, wish I was one of those morning people I'm passing that didn't have to go to work.

Arrive at the workplace, look for decent parking, tie up the bike. Remember to clean glasses finally, rub some more sleep from my eye. Make a beeline through the door to my coffee cup. Remedy it's emptiness promptly while grunting greetings to the crew in passing. Punch the clock, pace around for 5 minutes deciding what to do.

Work my ass off for 2 hours, grab a warm breakfast with OJ, mess around on my phone, catch up on Voat, savoring every moment. Work another 2 hours, very busy now, where does the time go, coffee long gone, on my 3rd piece of gum. Take a power nap anywhere I can, try and eat something so I can stay awake later.

Morning over, the day expands. Starting to feel alert and productive, decisions are made, routines done. Play some music loud and finish up, bullshitting with people, looking forward to the rest of the day. Hit the clock, grab some lunch and a 6 pack, roll on home.

Back home, open up the windows some more, turn on the computer, charge up the cell. Take care of business in the men's room, crack a beer, unwrap that sandwich. Catch up on Voat. Play a few games of League of Legends, or maybe Magic: The Gathering. Crank the tunes a little more while it's still light out and swing some kettlebells, do some pullups, squats, pushups, maybe some Hun Gar stance training. Try to remember exercises from gym class. Maybe rub one out, maybe not, I'm getting old. Play that song again, hit the shower.

Heat up dinner, queue up Netflix, miss my old boo a minute, then laugh at Sterling Archer and nod at Alton Brown. Fire up League again, try and climb the ladder, really diggin that Pandora mix about now. Drinking whiskey and bitters, trying not to watch the clock, I can always sleep on lunch break tomorrow.
